title: Wellington T2962
cause_of_loss: Starboard engine failure; struck trees attempting forced landing
memorial_details: Rectangular, bronze plaque with a dark, textured background with a narrow border and lettering in smooth bronze relief.
inscription: IN MEMORY OF/ (military names)/ AND/ (civilian names)/ DIED IN LLANGROVE AS A RESULT OF/ THE WELLINGTON BOMBER CRASH/ 7 JULY 1942

sources.title: Facebook post by Tony Hibberd (admin, RAF Bomber Command Memorials group), citing Chorley BCL Vol 7

narrative: Attempting a forced landing, the aircraft struck trees, lost a wing, and crashed and burned near Christ Church, Llangrove, at approximately 17:00. Two of the crew were killed and four were injured. The crash had devastating consequences beyond the aircrew: the village church organist collapsed and died of a heart attack while carrying water to fight the fire; the vicar, cycling home after returning to the scene to administer last rites, also died of a heart attack. Their names appear on the memorial plaque alongside those of the military dead.
community_connection: Two Llangrove civilians died as a direct result of the crash: the church organist collapsed and died of a heart attack while carrying water to fight the fire; the vicar, who had cycled to the scene to administer last rites, also died of a heart attack cycling home afterwards. Their names appear on the plaque alongside the military dead — an unusually direct record of civilian grief.
